gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ his temper in the meeting yesterday.
gaps.hint: past regret with wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect: had not lost.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ the lottery, she would travel the world.
gaps.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: If they ___ us about the delay, we would still be waiting at the airport.
gaps.hint: past cause with a result right now
gaps.explanation: A past unreal condition with a present result is a mixed conditional: had not told.
